meta.name: Create Shopify product video ads from your catalog with Zvid bulk rendering

parameters.content:
## Start and configure

Provides manual and scheduled entry points, then centralizes workflow settings such as Shopify, render, dry-run, and delivery options.

## Fetch Shopify catalog

Retrieves product catalog data from Shopify using the configuration prepared at the start of the workflow.

## Create ad candidates

Turns catalog data into ad concepts, checks whether any ads were produced, and either builds the ad template or ends with a no-work summary.

## Validate render project

Validates the generated Zvid project, checks the validation result, and decides whether to continue through dry-run or real rendering.

## Save dry run

For dry-run executions, saves the generated draft to the editor and produces a dry-run summary without submitting renders.

## Submit render batch

Submits the generated ads as a bulk render job and verifies that the batch was accepted before polling begins.

## Poll render status

Waits between checks, requests the latest batch status, branches when rendering is complete, and loops while the batch is still in progress or fails fast when needed.

## Collect and preview

Collects completed rendered ad outputs and provides a nearby direct video request path for watching an individual rendered video.

## Prepare delivery manifest

Builds the delivery manifest from rendered outputs and checks whether an external delivery destination has been configured.

## Deliver or review

If delivery is configured, posts the manifest to an external asset store or scheduler and summarizes the result; otherwise returns a review-only summary for the rendered assets.

parameters.content:
## Dynamic Product Ad Factory

Reads selected Shopify products, creates product-first, benefit-first, and offer-first concepts, renders them as one Zvid bulk job, and builds a scheduler-neutral delivery/performance manifest.

### Required community node
Before configuring credentials or running the workflow, open **Settings → Community nodes → Install** and install the exact package **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**. A workspace owner or admin may need to do this.

**Safe first run:** `dryRun` defaults to `true`. Validation and the editor draft are free. Set it to `false` only after checking the quote and preview.

This workflow is intentionally independent and contains all setup instructions on its canvas. Shopify access is **read-only**: it reads catalog data but does not attach videos to products. Leave `deliveryWebhookUrl` blank unless you have an asset store or scheduler ready.

## 1 · Create a Shopify app (2026+)

In Shopify Admin open **Settings → Apps → Develop apps → Build apps in Dev Dashboard**. In Dev Dashboard:
1. Select **Apps → Create app → Start from Dev Dashboard**.
2. Name the app.
3. Open **Versions** and create a version.
4. For an API-only app, keep Shopify's default app-home URL.
5. Add only the Admin API scope **`read_products`**.
6. Select **Release**.
7. Open **Home → Install app**, select the store, and approve installation.

New custom apps can no longer be created directly in Shopify Admin. Existing admin-created apps may continue using their installed Admin API token.

Official guide: https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/dev-dashboard/create-apps-using-dev-dashboard

## 2 · Get `X-Shopify-Access-Token`

The Client ID and Client secret are **not** the access token. In Dev Dashboard open the app → **Settings**, copy both, then exchange them:

```bash
curl -X POST \
  https://YOUR_STORE.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  -d 'client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID' \
  -d 'client_secret=YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET'
```

Copy `access_token` from the JSON response. Never paste the Client secret into this workflow JSON. Dev Dashboard client-credentials tokens expire after **24 hours**; request a new token and update the n8n credential before a later run. For unattended scheduling, implement secure token refresh. The client-credentials grant is for an app and store owned by the same Shopify organization; use Shopify's OAuth installation flow for other merchants.

Official guide: https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/dev-dashboard/get-api-access-tokens?lang=curl

## 3 · Connect Shopify in n8n

Open **Credentials → New credential → Header Auth** and enter:
- **Name:** `X-Shopify-Access-Token`
- **Value:** the returned `access_token`

Open **Get Shopify catalog**, choose that credential, and save the node.

In **Config** set:
- `shopDomain`: prefix only; use `example` for `example.myshopify.com`
- `shopifyProductQuery`: default `status:active`; change it to target a vendor, tag, product type, or another Shopify Admin filter
- `scanLimit`: products fetched from Shopify
- `maxProducts`: eligible products selected
- `variantsPerProduct`: maximum variants for each selected product
- `maxTotalAds`: total video cap across all products

The planner allocates one variant to each selected product before starting the second round. For 2 products × 2 variants, set `maxTotalAds` to 4. Set it to 2 for one variant per product.

A `401 Unauthorized` usually means the wrong value was used or the 24-hour token expired. A `403` usually means `read_products` was not granted or the new app version was not approved.

## 4 · Install and connect Zvid

The Zvid nodes are supplied by a community package and are required by this workflow. Before running it:
1. Open **Settings → Community nodes** in n8n.
2. Select **Install**.
3. Enter the exact package name **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**.
4. Confirm the installation. If you cannot install community nodes, ask the n8n workspace owner or admin.

Create an API key at **https://app.zvid.io/api-keys**. In n8n create a **Zvid API** credential and enter:
- **API Key:** your `zvid_…` key
- **Base URL:** keep `https://api.zvid.io`

Assign the same credential to all four native Zvid nodes:
- **Validate project (free)** — Render → Validate
- **Save draft to editor** — Project → Create Editor Project
- **Submit bulk render** — Render → Create Bulk
- **Get batch status** — Render → Get Bulk

Then set your brand, website, colors, CTA, and optional licensed `musicUrl` in **Config**. Keep `dryRun: true`, run **Test manually**, review the exact credit quote and editor link, then set it to `false` to render.

## Concept matrix

For each selected product the workflow rotates through:
1. **product-first** — product-led headline and price context
2. **benefit-first** — benefit headline and Shopify description
3. **offer-first** — price or real compare-at savings

Each format supplies distinct opener, story, benefit, and offer copy to Zvid. The planner uses round-robin allocation across products: every selected product receives its first variant before any product receives a second. The total is capped by `maxTotalAds` (default 5).

Example: `maxProducts: 2`, `variantsPerProduct: 2`, `maxTotalAds: 4` creates 4 ads. A total cap of 2 creates 2 ads: one per product.

No unsupported discount is invented. Shopify's product connection does not support `BEST_SELLING`; use `UPDATED_AT` plus your query or feed it sales-ranked IDs from another workflow.

## Delivery contract

Leave `deliveryWebhookUrl` blank to receive review links in n8n. Add an HTTPS endpoint only when it is ready to accept one JSON manifest containing every rendered asset. Add any destination credential to **Send to asset store or scheduler**.

Each asset includes a stable `trackingKey`, Shopify product ID/URL, format, hook, offer, video URL, job ID, and zeroed performance fields. Store the tracking key beside the platform post/ad ID so a later reporting workflow can join metrics to the exact creative.

This template does **not** publish an ad or collect live metrics by itself. It hands off assets and a tracking contract to the destination. With no webhook, the tested review branch returns all URLs and plays the MP4s inside n8n.

## Approved Atelier Editorial design

A product such as **Harbor Stripe Breton Tee — Navy & Ivory** at **$36** produces up to three editorial variants:
- Product-first: direct new-edit framing
- Benefit-first: description-led benefits
- Offer-first: price or real compare-at savings

The design uses up to three Shopify images across an image-led opener, product story, benefits, offer, and CTA. If only one image exists, it is safely reused. The first scene uses a full-frame dark wash plus a strong bottom gradient; the second uses a dark two-axis overlay behind white copy. The end-card brand sits inside a wide bordered capsule that accommodates realistic brand names.

The design resolves to about **18.9 seconds** with two benefit cards. Always use the free validation quote returned by your own dry run before rendering.
